Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines — subprocessor chain / data deletion question

Hi Irene / Dev —

Attached are the redlines our Legal team proposed to the MSA and the new Order Form. Two items in particular we need to resolve before procurement can sign:

1) Subprocessor flow-down: we want mandatory flow-down language requiring that any subcontractor who processes customer data must accept the same data obligations (including deletion on termination) and provide written evidence of compliance on request.

2) Chain-of-custody & transfers: a clause that requires notification and a 30-day objection window before the Supplier (you) can engage a third-party subprocessor in a country outside the EU/US.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can (a) provide subprocessor attestations (template) and (b) accept the 30-day notification window? If not, what alternate language would you propose?

We attached the redlines: Acme_MSA_redlines_2026-07-22.pdf and the updated order form.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if easier.

Sasha Miller

Subject: RE: Fwd: MSA + Order Form redlines — subprocessor chain / data deletion question

Irene / team — reviewed Acme's redlines and drafted two alternatives. High-level:

Option A (Enterprise / Customer-required):
- Accepts explicit flow-down: any subprocessor who accesses customer data must enter into a written agreement that mirrors the data protection obligations in the MSA (including deletion on termination).
- Adds a 30-calendar-day notice to the customer before engaging a subprocessor in a new country; the customer may object for reasonable security/compliance reasons.
- Requires that, upon request, the Supplier provide a signed attestation from the subprocessor and evidence of contractual flow-down.

Operational impact: Ops must maintain a subprocessor inventory and be prepared to produce attestations within 10 business days of request. 30-day notice could slow onboarding of some capacity partners — propose implementing a standard exception process for emergency scaling (subject to security review).

Option B (Standard / Sales-friendly):
- Commit to using commercially reasonable efforts to flow down obligations to subprocessors, provide a current subprocessor list, and deliver attestations upon request within a reasonable timeframe (15 business days).
- Replace the 30-day approval with a 10-business-day notification window and a requirement to provide relevant security artifacts for the subprocessor.

Recommended approach: Accept Option B for all hosted and standard Order Forms; reserve Option A for Dedicated or regulated enterprise customers with explicit annexes. That keeps procurement moving while preserving stronger controls where it's required.

Attached: Proposed_Subprocessor_Clause_v1.docx (redline + clean). Also suggested edits to OrderForm_Acme_v2.docx to reference our Subprocessor Appendix.

If you want, I can draft a short email to Acme summarizing the compromise language and next steps (DocuSign for order form + MSA appendix).

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Proposed_Subprocessor_Clause_v1.docx]

1) Attestation turnaround: can Legal commit to 15 business days maximum for a signed subprocessor attestation? That implies we need a standard attestation template and a tracked inbox for requests.
2) Emergency scaling exception: if we allow a security-reviewed exception for emergency scaling, we need a template SLA (30 days post-deployment to get the attestation). Can Legal draft the exception text we can show customers?

If Legal can provide the templates, I can work with infra to confirm we can meet the timelines and bake this into our onboarding checklist. Happy to jump on a 20-min sync with Acme if useful.

Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form redlines — subprocessor chain / data deletion question

Sasha — thanks for the clear redlines and callout. We discussed internally and propose the following compromise to keep procurement moving: 

1) For the attached Order Form we can adopt the sales-friendly variant (Option B): Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to flow down the data obligations to subprocessors, provide a current subprocessor list, and deliver signed attestations on request within 15 business days.

2) For Dedicated or regulated deployments (enterprise deals) we are willing to accept the stronger Option A language, with a 30-calendar-day notice window before engaging subprocessors in new jurisdictions and a contractual right to objection for reasonable security/compliance concerns.

3) Emergency scaling: we agree to a documented exception process — Redwood will notify the customer within 48 hours of an emergency subprocessor engagement and deliver the attestation within 30 days, subject to a security review.

Next steps:
- I asked Legal to attach the proposed clause and the edited Order Form (see attachments).
- If that works for Acme, we'll send a short mutual action plan and a DocuSign packet for the Order Form + MSA amendment. Link to draft MAP: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cAcmeReview

Please confirm and we can schedule a 20-min call this week if you prefer to walk through.

Best,
Irene Choi
